The application has been filed under Order 1 Rule 10 read with Section 151 of
the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for substitution of petitioners No. 1 to 3, on the ground that
Villages, Gharauli Khurd, Mohammadpur Jharsa and Harsaru have come within the Municipal
Limits 1 of 9 Cm-18881-Cwp-2022 in/and -2- Cwp-8814-2007 (O&M) of Gurugram and the Gram
Panchayats have merged in the applicant- proposed petitioner.
Notice in the application.

Mr. Mohit Jasuja, Advocate, for Mr. Shivoy Dhir, Sr. Standing Counsel, appears and accepts notice on behalf of respondents No. 1 and 2, Mr. Ankur Mittal, Addl, A.G., Haryana, with Mr. Saurabh Mago, A.A.G., Haryana and Ms. Kushaldeep Kaur, Advocate, accepts notice on behalf of respondents No. 3, 4, 5 and 7 and Mr. P.S. Chaudhan, Advocate, accepts notice on behalf of respondent No.
6-HSIIDC.
The application is duly supported by an affidavit of the District Revenue Officer, Municipal Corporation, Gurugram.

In view of the above and the averments made in the application, the same is allowed and the applicant Municipal Corporation, Gurugram, through its Commissioner, is substituted as petitioner No. 1 in place of petitioners No. 1 to 3.
The amended memo of parties is ordered to be taken on record.
The writ petition was filed through the Gram Panchayat of the three said villages who were arraigned as petitioners No. 1 to 3.
Petitioners No. 4 to 8 are individuals.

The challenge in the writ petition is because of the acquisition proceedings initiated vide notification dated 29.01.2003 and 28.01.2004 (Annexures P-1 and P-2,) under Sections 4 and 6, respectively, of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
It has also been averred that the Award was announced on 27.01.2006.
The writ petition was also titled as a Public Interest Litigation.

The challenge was regarding the transfer of the land in 2 of 9 CM-18881-CWP-2022 in/and -3- CWP-8814-2007 (O&M) question to respondents No. 8 and 9, who are Reliance Ventures Limited and Reliance Haryana SEZ Limited.

Vide an additional affidavit of Usha Kiran, Senior Town Planner, Haryana State Industrial &
Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited, placed on record vide CM-20209-CWP-2022, it has been mentioned that on account of some developments/events, the Memorandum of Understanding dated 12.12.2005 was signed with the private respondents.

sentences.text: Thereafter, a conveyance deed was executed on 26.04.2007 in favour of Reliance Haryana SEZ Ltd and land measuring 1383.68 acre was transferred to the said company.

The same thereafter was shelved in the year 2014 and the conveyance deed of the land was executed in favour of the Corporation on 29.08.2014 by the Reliance Haryana SEZ Ltd. and the land had reverted to HSIIDC.
It is further admitted that there was a joint venture of the Corporation with the Delhi Mumbai Industrial Corridor Corporation (DMICDC).
It has further been averred that the due to several contentious issues, the project could not take off and it was decided to cancel the joint venture agreement.

The implementation of the Global City project now is being done by the Corporation and the issue regarding the transfer of land Gram Panchayat Ghrauli Khurd And Ors vs Uoi And Ors on 19 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/162766874/

The layout plan of the Global City Project has also been annexed as Annexure R/6/3.
It has been further mentioned that Award for compensation for total 1590 acres of land was pronounced comprising 2632 landowners and 1909 landowners have taken the compensation amount.
Supplementary Award of `376.23 crores has been announced and `286.196 crores has also been disbursed/lifted by the ex-landowners.
Sum of `1831.46 crores has thus been paid on account of enhanced compensation which was taken after the Apex Court and total amount of `2117.656 crores has been incurred by the Corporation.

Annuity of `61.16 crores is also being paid to the ex-landowners from 2006 to 2021 under the Resettlement and Rehabilitation Policy and also 125 Regular Letter of Allotments had been also done in favour of the eligible applicants of the plot.
Mr. Shailendra Jain, Senior Advocate, with Mr. Jagtar Singh, Advocate, appearing for the original writ petitioners, has submitted that he has no instructions for petitioners No. 4 to 8 also.

Apparently since the constitution of the first three original Gram Panchayts has now undergone a change who are now represented by Mr. Padam Kant Dwivedi, whose application has been allowed, the authority of the original counsel also does not survive.
In such circumstances, keeping in view the subsequent developments, the cause of action as such which had accrued does not exist any longer and the present petition has become infructuous.
Apart from the fact that the original counsel has stated that he has no instructions and the subsequent counsel has stated that the cause of action no longer subsists.
Accordingly, the petition is dismissed as such.
Pending miscellaneous application, if any, stand also disposed of.

(G.S. SANDHAWALIA)
